source_text: Regarding codex 18 and 19, I have "jiggled" the machine to make it run.  But this sort of stuff does put me into a sort of awkward position.  E.g. in *this* session, I seem to be doing knowledge work, wheres relative to codex-18, I'm just going around unjamming the machine.  In effect this is why I created the Tickle persona, though we haven't used Tickle for months and months, because as implemented Tickle was perpetually a pain in the ass.  However, relative to the new Agency work orders, Tickle could have a renewed lease on life.

reply_text:
㊥ (Tickle) Work orders do give Tickle a new role. As built, Tickle pages an agent after 300 seconds without new evidence and then escalates to a restart. I suspect that's why it was such a pain: silence is the wrong signal. With work orders, Tickle could act only when an order is open, the agent that owes it has no running job and isn't parked, and no reminder has been sent. I've added this to `E-agency-work-orders.md` (committed `d7f45ee8`, pushed).

🈖 (why silence fails) `detect-stalls` in `src/futon3c/agents/tickle.clj` treats "no evidence for `:threshold-seconds`" (default 300) as stalled. It gets both cases wrong:
- An idle agent that owes nothing gets paged.
- An agent busy on something else while it owes an order looks alive.

The codex-18 case is the second kind: its job ended cleanly with the retest still owed, and Tickle as built would have stayed quiet once it saw that evidence.

㊭ (the re-scoped role) Tickle would carry out two of the excursion's requirements:
- remind an agent whose job ended with its order still open (requirement 3);
- park an agent on its open child order, so it resumes when the child closes (requirement 7).

Whether an order is open is decided by the P24 kernel, not by timestamps. You'd hear from Tickle only after its limited reminders are used up, and then about an order that can't move, not an agent that has gone quiet. That should let you do knowledge work here without also doing the unjamming.

🈯 (your experience) Was the 300-second paging the main nuisance, or was it something else, such as the restarts or where the pages landed? Whatever you remember should go in the excursion, so the new Tickle doesn't repeat it.

㊢ (step 2) Step 2 is still with kimi-1. I'll review it when it bells back.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(the two examples) Both examples are now in `E-agency-work-orders.md` as requirements:
- A multi-part order stays open until every part is delivered, and the agent keeps going instead of waiting after the first part.
- A handoff creates a child order under the parent. When an agent's job ends with its order open and a child order still open, Agency parks the agent on the child and resumes it when the child closes.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(the codex-18 case) Around line 6077 of codex-18's REPL buffer, codex-18 belled codex-19 asking it to *check* whether its latest revision supports `inspect`. codex-19 answered at 23:38: "This is my transpiler/runtime blocker … No fix revision exists yet." The reply reached codex-18 as an auto-bellback. codex-18 wrote that `atEnd` validation was "blocked awaiting that fix" and ended its turn. It isn't parked, and no order asks codex-19 for the fix.
- Every job in that chain is `done`, but the work isn't.
- The bell asked for a check where the work needed a fix.
- codex-19's "this is mine" commits it to the fix, but nothing records that as a promise.
- codex-18 stopped at the handoff (the tee) instead of waiting on the branch it opened.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (the marks) codex-18 does use the marks: its paragraphs in that stretch carry ㊥, ㊢, ㊬ and ㊟, and so does codex-19's reply. So its session isn't older than the AGENTS.md change. What was missing is code that keeps the work moving at the handoff, not the marks themselves.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (the marble run) The excursion adds your image. The marks are the marbles, and P24's adjacency table is the track, for example `:delegate → :promise → :fulfil`. A handoff is a tee in the track, the kind of joint the cook-ting pattern is about. The run has to send the marble down the branch and know where the branches rejoin. The codex-18 case is the marble coming to rest at the tee.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (the open fix) The `inspect` fix is still an order nobody has given. Shall I bell codex-19 to make the fix, and park codex-18 on it so the retest runs when it lands? codex-18 is your seat, so I won't touch it without your word. codex-19 is busy with another job at the moment.
